findings.reason: Confirmed. At Mathlib 082e2d3, ContRepresentation (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Continuous/Basic.lean:54; declarations.tsv agrees) is a structure whose only field is toMonoidHom : G →* V →L[R] V, under [Monoid G] with no TopologicalSpace G; the module docstring (lines 21-25) says the action of G on V is not assumed continuous. So it gives continuity of each operator ρ(g) only. For a representation of a Galois group on a finite-dimensional space over a finite extension of Q_p that condition is automatic, and the continuity R24.2 asks for ('the induced representation is continuous') is joint continuity in the group variable, which ContRepresentation does not express. The audit's 'which is the right ambient notion' is therefore false as stated. TopRep (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Continuous/TopRep.lean:31) carries a ContRepresentation and has the same limitation, so the red team is right that it is no replacement. Action.IsContinuous (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Action/Continuous.lean:60) is ContinuousSMul G on the underlying space, under [TopologicalSpace G] and [HasForget₂ V TopCat], and ContAction (:74) is the full subcategory of such actions; these express group-variable continuity generically but carry no Galois or deformation data. REV-AUDIT-34 made no correction here. Fix scope: rewrite the note of PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.2 target 1 (zero-based) to say ContRepresentation supplies continuous linear operators only, that continuity of the Galois action in the group variable is not expressed by it, and that neither the continuity condition for the representation carried by a deformation-ring point nor its verification exists. Action.IsContinuous (:60) and ContAction (:74) may be added as related, with their hypotheses (topology on G, concrete category over TopCat), giving at most three declarations. Keep ContRepresentation as related, the target partial and R24.2 not built. The same wording qualification (operators only, no group-variable continuity) may be applied to the ContRepresentation clause of the PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5 target 0 note, which groups it with 'continuous Galois representations', and to the parenthetical in the SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation summary; no status, citation or verdict changes there. Disclosure: PA.5 is a potential-automorphy stage; see the report.

Confirmed. The only declaration cited for PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.2 target 4 (zero-based) is CategoryTheory.Limits.lim (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/HasLimits.lean:541; declarations.tsv agrees), the ordinary limit functor (J ⥤ C) ⥤ C, F ↦ limit F, under [HasLimitsOfShape J C]. It has no derived functors and no tower bound. A search of both pinned trees for lim¹, derived or inverse-limit control, Rlim and Milnor sequences finds nothing; Mittag-Leffler appears only in CategoryTheory/CofilteredSystem.lean (IsMittagLeffler at :137 for functors to Type, eventual ranges and nonempty sections), and RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Exactness.lean states it avoids Mittag-Leffler systems. So the note's 'generic derived-limit ... machinery exists in Mathlib' is not supported by the citation and claims more than the pins give. Against the red team: Mathlib does have the generic right-derived-functor framework, CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerived (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/RightDerived.lean:109) for an additive functor on an abelian category with enough injectives, from which R^n lim could be formed, so the fix must not claim derived functors are absent (the red team says the same). The red team's 'TC.2 target 3' is one-based; zero-based it is TC.2 target 2. Fix scope: rewrite only the PA.2 target 4 note to credit the ordinary limit functor and the generic derived-functor and finite-generation groundwork, and to state that no derived tower-limit API, no lim¹ vanishing or Mittag-Leffler criterion for modules, and none of the vanishing, control, duality or finite-generation bounds PA.2 asks for exists at the pins. Keep the lim citation; Functor.rightDerived (:109) may be added as related (two declarations). Target partial, PA.2 not built and the PA summary are unchanged. Disclosure: PA.2 is a potential-automorphy stage; see the report.

Confirmed. Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean at 082e2d3, under the file variables CommRing R, p prime, Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R) and IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R, defines fontaineThetaInvertP (:64), BDeRhamPlus (:77), the adic completion of Localization.Away (p : W(R♭)) at ker fontaineThetaInvertP, and BDeRham (:90); declarations.tsv gives the same lines. The module docstring lists both period rings as main definitions and leaves the extension of θ, the DVR property and principality of ker θ as TODO. So the note of PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.6 target 3 (zero-based), that the file 'builds only the first step towards B_dR', is false. One correction to the red team's description: BDeRham localises BDeRhamPlus at the submonoid generated by the images of the elements a with ker θ = span {a}, that is, single generators of ker θ; when ker θ is not principal that set is empty and nothing is inverted. The docstrings also note that both rings are zero when p = 0 in R. No D_dR, de Rham representation, Weil-Deligne representation or lifting theorem exists in either library (searched for DeRham, de Rham and Weil-Deligne). Fix scope: add BDeRhamPlus (:77) and BDeRham (:90) as related citations beside fontaineThetaInvertP (three declarations), and rewrite the note to credit these definitions with their hypotheses and the limits of their API (no θ on B_dR^+, no DVR or principality result, generator-based localisation). Target stays absent and R24.6 not built; do not present period-ring definitions as a comparison theorem or as representation theory.

Confirmed. The audit's duplicate entry AutomorphicCongruences:L0 on SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.1 says L0 'owns the congruence-module construction R20.1 also requests'. The L0 stage text opens 'Import congruence ideals/modules, generalized matrix algebras, pseudorepresentations, reducibility ideals and the general extension-class construction from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants', and keeps for itself only their source-specific relation to the chosen periods and the actual automorphic extension classes. The AutomorphicCongruences document's scope says 'Generic pseudorepresentations, reducibility/congruence ideals and extension classes are owned by IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants'. So the ownership claim is wrong. IHG.1 is the right general stage: 'Develop reducibility ideals, extension modules and the lattice constructions used by congruence arguments.' Against the red team: IHG.1's text does not name congruence modules explicitly, and the IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants packet on main has IHG.1 nodes only for Cayley-Hamilton algebras. IHG.5's congruence clause concerns local conditions of extension classes and lattice choices, which R20.1 does not ask for, so IHG.5 is not relevant to R20.1. No congruence module or congruence ideal exists in either pinned library (searched), so the target stays absent. Fix scope: rewrite the L0 entry of R20.1's duplicates as a consumer overlap. It applies the imported general congruence modules to automorphic periods and extension classes, and does not own them. Add IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1 as the general supplier, noting that its text names reducibility ideals, extension modules and lattice constructions and not congruence modules by name. Do not add IHG.5. Do not add packet requests in the audit fix: a finer owner node belongs to the IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants packet work. R20.1's targets, statuses and the not built verdict are unchanged.
